draft.title: Establishment and growth
card: The business life cycle describes the stages a business moves through over time. The first two stages are establishment and growth.
the start-up stage. Sales are low, costs are high, and the owner often struggles to keep enough cash coming in to pay bills.
This stage is risky. Many new businesses run short of cash before they build a steady base of customers.
sales and profits rise, and the business hires more staff. The owner now faces new challenges in managing people and in finding finance to expand.
draft.remember: Establishment is risky with low sales. Growth brings rising sales and new management and finance demands.

a.q: Which description best fits a business in the establishment stage?
opts: Low sales and trouble paying bills on time
Rising profits and a growing team of staff
Sales that have stopped rising or falling
Plans to introduce new products to old customers
a.why: In establishment, sales are low and cash flow is a common problem. Rising profits and more staff belong to growth, which is the tempting wrong answer because it is also an early stage.
a.clue: Think about the start-up stage, when few customers know the business.

b.q: Priya's bakery in Wagga Wagga now sells more each month and has hired four staff. She says rostering and finding money for a second oven are her biggest worries. Which stage is it in, and why?
opts: Growth, because sales are rising and demands are new
Establishment, because the owner is worried about money
Growth, because the business no longer faces any risk
Establishment, because the business has hired staff
b.why: Rising sales, new staff and the need for finance to expand are signs of growth. Worry about money alone does not mean establishment, as growth brings finance challenges too.
b.clue: Rising sales and extra staff point to one stage, and money worries can appear in both.

a.best: Low sales and trouble paying bills on time

b.best: Growth, because sales are rising and demands are new

problems.detail: The clue 'Think about the start-up stage, when few customers know the business' points straight at the low-sales answer and gives it away.
